portfolio_view: All five are Stage-2 breakouts with accelerating earnings and rising FII/DII ownership, but each clears the mechanical score with a genuine, verified company- or order-book-specific driver rather than pure momentum. Diversified one-per-sector across Healthcare (Neuland), Financial Services (MCX), Utilities/Water (Wabag), Auto Components (Belrise) and Capital Goods/Defence (Paras). Market regime is NORMAL (56.2% above 200-DMA) so full sizing applies, but stay selective on entries. Two daily-analyst BUYs were passed over: LAURUSLABS (BUY, MEDIUM/HALF) duplicates Neuland's Pharma CDMO exposure with a weaker conviction signal (HIGH/FULL vs MEDIUM/HALF); EIMCOELECO (BUY, MEDIUM/HALF) has the weakest RS (74) in the whole candidate set and duplicates Paras's Capital Goods slot.
theme_read: Pharma CDMO & API (heat 79, hottest) has heat that matches price — 3m return of 12.2% shows this is already running, confirmed by Neuland's genuine margin re-rating and India's rising share of US FDA DMF filings, though the correlated Dec-2024 CDMO selloff is a reminder the group can de-rate together. Water, environment & EPC (heat 75, 2nd-hottest, widest actionable breadth) is a case of news running ahead of price, not the reverse: Wabag's record order book and international wins kept landing through mid-2026 even as the theme's 3m return went negative on a broad sector pullback — the heat looks "late" but may still be underpriced. EV & auto electrification (heat 68, flagged as strengthening on PM E-DRIVE) is where mechanical heat is most misleading: the real beneficiaries are Ola Electric, Ather Energy and Exide (outside this pool), and Belrise's presence in the confirmed list overstates its actual EV exposure — the pick is really a 2W-content story wearing an EV label. Defence & aerospace and Defence electronics & space (heat 62/42.3) are genuinely strengthening on export-SOP liberalization, but that named driver's beneficiaries (BDL, MIDHANI, Data Patterns) sit outside this pool — Paras's own catalyst is real but distinct. Financial market infrastructure (heat 67.3, flat) is where MCX sits, though its story is idiosyncratic to commodity-derivative volumes and a favorable STT differential, not a broad infra re-rating.
